plan: The dominant strategy in this auction is to bid your value. This is because, if you bid less than your value, you risk losing the auction to someone who values the item more, and you miss out on potential profit. If you bid more than your value, you risk winning the auction and incurring a loss. Since this is round 1 of 1, and there's no prior history, I will follow the dominant strategy.

The dominant strategy in a second-price sealed-bid auction is to bid your true value. This is because you only pay the second-highest bid, so there's no downside to bidding truthfully. Bidding less risks losing the item even if it's worth more to you, and bidding more doesn't change the amount you pay if you win. My value is $44, so I will bid $44.

The dominant strategy in this second-price sealed-bid auction is to bid your true value. This is because you want to win if and only if your value exceeds the second-highest bid. Bidding less than your value risks losing the auction to someone who values the item more, and bidding more than your value risks winning the auction but paying more than the item is worth to you. My value is $43, so I will bid $43.
